speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you are a child presenting with frequent nosebleeds, bleeding from your mucous membranes, and small red spots on your skin called petechiae. To understand what is causing this, have you noticed if these symptoms get worse after you play sports, run, or have any bumps and bruises recently?

speaker: Patient
text: 4-year-old male. The child's parent reports that the child has been experiencing frequent episodes of nosebleeds and has had several instances of bleeding from the gums. Additionally, there have been occurrences of unexplained bruising and petechiae, primarily on the distal extremities.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Immune Thrombocytopenia (ITP).

The history of frequent epistaxis, gum bleeding, unexplained bruising, and petechiae specifically on the distal extremities in a 4-year-old male is classic for this condition. I need to confirm the platelet count and rule out other causes; REQUEST TEST: Complete_Blood_Count_with_Platelets, REQUEST TEST: Peripheral_Blood_Smear.
